original_forecast.resolution_rule: Resolve against front-month NYMEX WTI settlement, using a consistent roll convention documented at resolution.
rationale: Weak labor data creates easing pressure.
Inflation/geopolitical risk remains large enough to prevent a narrow forecast.
Cross-asset confirmation is more informative than SPX alone.
surprising_if: Outcome falls outside the stated 80% interval or materially contradicts the linked causal story.

resolution.source: Reuters Sep. 8, 2026 oil-market close, reporting the active front-month U.S. West Texas Intermediate futures settlement.
resolution.roll_convention: Use the active front-month NYMEX WTI contract as quoted in Reuters' Sep. 8 settlement report; no bespoke roll adjustment is introduced at resolution.
resolution.audit_note: Original forecast content is preserved without hindsight alteration. The $93.03 settlement was $2.03 above the frozen $91 upper bound, so the stated 80% interval missed and the precommitted surprising condition fired. The $78.00 point also lost slightly to frozen no-change. This is a genuine distributional/tail miss. It is preserved prominently, but one miss from an 80% interval does not by itself justify retroactively widening the model's uncertainty bands or changing the causal graph.
